messages:
Ashley (support): FYI we just got a high-severity from AcmeCorp — p95/p99 for generate API jumped ~3-4x after we onboarded model xqa-v2 last night. They see big spikes on long-context jobs (~8k tokens). Ticket: https://acme.support/INC-3122 :cry:

Jordan (ml-eng): Ugh. Did we change the tokenizer or just the model weights for v2? Any diffs in token counts for same prompts?

Ashley (support): Customer sent sample payloads. Short prompts are fine, but anything >= 4k tokens gets awful latency. They said tokens sometimes balloon compared to xqa-v1.

Mike (runtime): I'm seeing a cluster-level p99 increase starting at 2026-03-10T02:18Z that lines up with the xqa-v2 rollout. CPU for the router proxies spiked too. Could be KV cache churn or attention kernel falling back to slower path when sequence length distribution changed.

Priya (infra): Autoscaling didn't trigger for a subset of Dedicated pools because the rollout pinned model to node IDs (we tested sticky allocation). Checking pool utilization now.

SRE Bot: ALERT #ABC-9876 - generate.p99 > 1200ms for support:d-us-east-1 between 02:18 and 03:05 UTC. Related traces: https://tracing.redwood/srv/abc-9876

Jordan (ml-eng): Can we get a repro? Ashley, can you paste one of the offending prompts and tokenizer counts? Also need model config: context window, tokenizer version, and whether we enabled any new quantization path.

Ashley (support): Repro snippet from customer (they redacted PII):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "xqa-v2",
  "input": "<~6k-token long doc> + few-shot Q/A",
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "stream": false
}
```
They included tokenization counts: v1 -> 5,900 tokens, v2 -> 8,300 tokens (same text).

Mike (runtime): That token delta screams tokenizer change. A 40% token inflation will push attention mem and cause the slower kernel selection. Jordan, did the tokenizer updates modify byte-pair merges or added sentinel tokens?

Jordan (ml-eng): Yes — when onboarding v2 we switched to a new SentencePiece model to better handle rare subwords and some language edgecases. We ran internal tests for quality, but looks like we missed long-document tokenization expansion cases. The tokenizer adds a lot more subword splits on long concatenated docs.

Priya (infra): I pulled pool logs. For the affected Dedicated pool we saw sustained GPU mem pressure and increased swap for the runtime process between 02:16 and 02:22Z while v2 served heavy requests. Autoscaler then tried to add nodes but allocation failed because of pinned instance constraints.

Ashley (support): Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they need SLA-level latency.

Jordan (ml-eng): Proposed mitigations (quick list):
- rollback tokenizer to v1 for xqa (pin tokenizer to xqa-v1-tokenizer while we investigate)
- enable route fallback: route long-context requests to xqa-v1 (compatible model variant) until we fix tokenization
- add input token limit on customer route (e.g., 6k) with clear error and suggestion to chunk
- improve prefix/KV caching warmup for xqa-v2 to reduce cold penalty

Mike (runtime): I can push a temporary routing rule that routes requests > 6k tokens to xqa-v1 for the AcmeCorp route only. That avoids cluster-wide disruption. Also we should disable the new persistence of KV across model variants for now (it was causing cache invalidations).

deploy-bot: Deployment queued by Mike. Rollout ID: r-20260310-02f. Canaries: 10% -> 50% -> 100% (target: support:d-us-east-1 route).

Ashley (support): Please make that targeted — customer confirmed they only want their traffic affected, not global.

Priya (infra): I'll temporarily relax the pinned instance constraint so autoscaler can spin up nodes if needed. Doing that now.

Mike (runtime): Rolling the route policy now, canary at 10% applied to AcmeCorp route.

SRE Bot: Deploy r-20260310-02f: canary 10% succeeded. Metrics: generate.p99 down from 1350ms -> 480ms for the canary subset.

Jordan (ml-eng): Good sign. I'll start generating tokenizer diffs and a small script to measure token inflation across a corpus. Quick check: here's a minimal repro tool to compare token counts locally:
```
python repro_token_diff.py --model v1-tokenizer.model --model2 v2-tokenizer.model --input sample_long_doc.txt
```
Output shows v1:5900, v2:8280 for the customer doc.

Ashley (support): Customer confirmed canary looks better. They're ok with a full rollback for them while we patch the tokenizer.

Mike (runtime): Pushing full route shift to 100% for AcmeCorp.

deploy-bot: Deployment r-20260310-02f: 100% complete. Rollback rule: none (this was an explicit targeted reroute).

SRE Bot: generate.p99 for AcmeCorp route returned to baseline (~420ms). Cluster-level p99 decreased ~20%.

Jordan (ml-eng): Action items:
- Jordan: prepare tokenizer patch that reduces BPE splits for long contexts; add regression tests on long-doc corpora (due EOD).
- Mike: add guardrail in runtime to detect sudden token inflation >25% vs baseline and emit a warning/metrics (due 48h).
- Priya: update autoscaler policy to ignore temporary pinned constraints during critical rollouts (due tomorrow morning).
- Ashley: coordinate with AcmeCorp about a timeline for full re-onboard once patched (ongoing).

Ashley (support): Customer happy with temporary fix, asked for post-mortem and timelines.

Jordan (ml-eng): I'll prototype tokenizer fix and run against a 5k-document corpus overnight. If pass, we can do a staged re-onboard with warmup and throttled rollout and monitoring.

Mike (runtime): For short-term platform protection, I'm going to add a runtime rule that forces kernel selection to the more robust attention implementation if seq_len > 6k to avoid falling into a slower fallback path. That should reduce p99 spikes vs unpredictable kernel combos.

Priya (infra): Noted. I'm also scheduling a maintenance window to remove the pinned-instance flag in prod for a while so autoscaler works during these kind of rollouts.

Ashley (support): Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and schedule a joint post-mortem once Jordan has the tokenizer patch results. :thumbsup:

Jordan (ml-eng): Uploading preliminary diffs and test results to the tokenization board: https://redwood.internal/boards/tokenizer/patch-312

Mike (runtime): Follow-ups: I'll add a dashboard tile for token-inflation-by-model and a trigger that notifies #eng-runtime if >30% inflation observed in a 15-min window.

Ashley (support): Closing loop for now, re-open if customer sees regression after changes.

Note: Recorded root cause: tokenizer model change caused token count inflation for long concatenated docs -> higher memory & kernel path change -> p95/p99 latency regression. Temporary mitigation: targeted routing rollback to xqa-v1 for the customer, autoscaler unpinned, planned tokenizer fix and runtime guardrails.
